Explorer.title: Cost of living explorer
Explorer.subtitle: Compare two countries on the costs that decide whether a move works.
Explorer.verdictCheaper: Living in {country} costs about {pct}% less than {source}.
Explorer.verdictPricier: Living in {country} costs about {pct}% more than {source}.
Explorer.verdictSame: Living costs in {country} and {source} are roughly the same.
Explorer.needed: To keep your current lifestyle in {country} you would need about {amount} per month.
Explorer.disclaimer: Figures are indicative averages for the capital or largest city and are meant for shortlisting, not budgeting to the last unit. Currency: USD.

Compare.quickPricier: Living in {to} costs about {percent}% more than {from}. The essential monthly budget for one person — rent in the city centre, groceries, utilities, transport and internet — comes to roughly {toCost} in {toCity} against {fromCost} in {fromCity}.
Compare.quickCheaper: Living in {to} costs about {percent}% less than {from}. The essential monthly budget for one person — rent in the city centre, groceries, utilities, transport and internet — comes to roughly {toCost} in {toCity} against {fromCost} in {fromCity}.
Compare.takeGap: The biggest single difference is {category}: {fromValue} in {fromCity} against {toValue} in {toCity}.
Compare.takeSalary: An average net salary in {to} ({salary}) covers about {ratio}× of the essential budget.
Compare.takeSalaryFrom: In {from} the same ratio is about {ratio}, which is what actually decides whether the move improves your monthly margin.
Compare.takeVisa: Cost is one input. {to} publishes {routes} main visa routes, and the requirements matter more than the price gap.
Compare.breakdownNote: All figures are monthly averages in US dollars for {toCity} and {fromCity}, so the two columns are directly comparable.
Compare.salaryBody: Average net salary is {toSalary} in {to} and {fromSalary} in {from}. Comparing prices without comparing pay is how a move that looks cheaper ends up tighter.
Compare.movingBody: The cost difference is one part of the decision. Visa eligibility, whether your qualification is recognised and whether employers sponsor are usually the parts that decide if the move is possible at all.
Compare.explorerLink: Adjust these figures with your own income
Compare.sourcesBody: Cost figures come from the datasets listed on our data page, and visa details from each country official immigration authority.
Compare.disclaimer: Figures are estimates for shortlisting, not quotes, and immigration rules change. Confirm with the official authority before acting.
Compare.metaPricier: {to} costs about {percent}% more than {from}: {toCost} vs {fromCost} a month for essentials. Compare rent, food, transport, salaries and visa routes.
Compare.metaCheaper: {to} costs about {percent}% less than {from}: {toCost} vs {fromCost} a month for essentials. Compare rent, food, transport, salaries and visa routes.
Compare.descTail1: Rent, food, transport, utilities, salaries and visa routes compared side by side.
Compare.descTail2: Rent, food, transport, salaries and visa routes compared.
Compare.descTail3: Rent, food, transport and salaries compared.
Compare.keywords: cost of living {to} vs {from}, moving from {from} to {to}, {to} salary vs {from}, {to} visa from {from}
Compare.descTail3b: A full monthly breakdown, side by side.
Compare.faqTitle: Common questions about moving from {from} to {to}
Compare.faqCostQPricier: How much more expensive is {to} than {from}?
Compare.faqCostAPricier: Essentials cost about {percent}% more in {to}. One person needs roughly {toCost} a month in {toCity} against {fromCost} in {fromCity}, covering rent in the city centre, groceries, utilities, a transport pass and internet.
Compare.faqCostACheaper: Essentials cost about {percent}% less in {to}. One person needs roughly {toCost} a month in {toCity} against {fromCost} in {fromCity}, covering rent in the city centre, groceries, utilities, a transport pass and internet.
Compare.faqBudgetQ: What is the estimated monthly budget in {to}?
Compare.faqBudgetA: About {toCost} a month for one person in {toCity}. That is rent for a one-bedroom in the city centre plus groceries, utilities, a public transport pass and internet. It excludes eating out, healthcare, childcare and one-off moving costs.
Compare.faqSalaryQ: Does an average salary in {to} cover the essentials?
Compare.faqSalaryA: An average net salary in {to} is {toSalary} a month and covers the {toCost} essential budget about {ratio} times over. In {from} the same ratio is about {fromRatio}. That comparison, not the price gap alone, is what decides whether the move improves your monthly margin.
Compare.faqGapQ: What is the biggest cost difference between {from} and {to}?
Compare.faqGapA: {category}: {fromValue} in {fromCity} against {toValue} in {toCity}. It is the single largest gap in the breakdown above, so it is the line to check first against real listings.
Compare.faqVisaQ: What visa do I need to move from {from} to {to}?
Compare.faqVisaA: {to} publishes {routes} main routes for work or residence, with requirements and processing times set out in the {to} guide. TRAVLBOK is not an immigration adviser, so confirm your eligibility with the official authority before acting.
Compare.driversDominant: Almost the whole difference is housing. Rent in the centre accounts for {share}% of the gap between {fromCity} and {toCity}; every other essential contributes far less.
Compare.driversLeading: Housing carries {share}% of the gap. The next largest contributor is {second}, at {secondRatio}× the {fromCity} figure.
Compare.driversShared: Housing carries {share}% of the gap, but it is not the whole story: {second} costs {secondRatio}× more in {toCity}, and {third} {thirdRatio}×.
Compare.driversNote: Shares are calculated over the five expenses in the essential budget — rent in the centre, groceries, utilities, transport and internet. The meal and outside-centre rows above are shown for context and are not counted twice.
Compare.outsideTitle: If you live outside the city centre
Compare.outsideNarrows: This is the one corridor here where living outside the centre closes part of the gap. The essential budget in {toCity} drops to {toCost} from {toCentre}, about {saving} less a month, and the difference against {fromCity} narrows from {centrePercent}% to {outsidePercent}%.
Compare.outsideUnchanged: Moving out of the centre barely changes this comparison. The essential budget in {toCity} becomes {toCost} instead of {toCentre}, and the gap stays close to where it was — {outsidePercent}% against {centrePercent}%.
Compare.outsideWidens: Rent outside the centre lowers the bill on both sides — but proportionally more in {fromCity}. The essential budget in {toCity} falls to {toCost} from {toCentre}, about {saving} less a month, while the gap against {fromCity} widens from {centrePercent}% to {outsidePercent}%.
Compare.outsideNote: Both sides use the outside-centre rent figure; every other expense is unchanged. A widening percentage does not mean the destination got more expensive — the destination bill falls, but the origin bill falls by a larger share.
Compare.reachTitle: How far your current pay goes
Compare.reachBody: One month of essentials in {toCity} costs about {months} months of the average net salary in {from} ({fromSalary}). This is a distance measure, not a budget: it says how far pay at home stretches there, not what you would earn after moving.
Compare.coverBelow: An average net salary in {to} ({toSalary}) does not by itself cover the essential budget of {toCost} — it comes to about {ratio}× it. {to} is the only destination in this pilot where the average net salary does not cover the essential monthly budget.
Compare.coverMarginal: An average net salary in {to} ({toSalary}) covers the {toCost} essential budget about {ratio}× over. That is a thin margin: the essentials are covered, but little else is.
Compare.coverComfortable: An average net salary in {to} ({toSalary}) covers the {toCost} essential budget about {ratio}× over, against about {fromRatio}× at home.
Compare.routesIntro: The routes covered in the {to} guide, with the processing times and government fees published there. {authority} is the authority that decides — confirm anything before acting on it.
Compare.routesIntroNoAuthority: The routes covered in the {to} guide, with the processing times and government fees published there. Confirm anything with the official immigration authority before acting on it.
Compare.needIntro: A selection of the requirements listed in the {to} guide. It is not a complete legal checklist — the full list, and the exceptions, are in the guide.
Compare.jobsIntro: Role types the {to} job data records as in demand, with the salary ranges and sponsorship patterns from that dataset. These are role archetypes and market signals, not live vacancies, and TRAVLBOK does not list employers.
Compare.showHousing: This corridor is a housing comparison more than a cost-of-living comparison: {share}% of the difference between {fromCity} and {toCity} is rent.
Compare.showHousingShared: Housing is {share}% of the difference between {fromCity} and {toCity}, with {second} a clear second at {secondRatio}× — a broader gap than most corridors on this site.
Compare.showReach: One month of essentials in {toCity} equals about {months} months of the average net salary in {from}.
Compare.showOutside: Taking rent outside the centre moves the gap from {centrePercent}% to {outsidePercent}%.
Compare.showCoverage: Locally, the destination average net salary covers the essential budget about {ratio}×.
Compare.limitsTitle: What this comparison does not tell you
Compare.limitEstimate: Every figure is an estimate for shortlisting, not a quote. Prices vary by neighbourhood, season and household size.
Compare.limitCore: The essential budget counts rent, groceries, utilities, transport and internet. It excludes eating out, health insurance, childcare, tax and one-off moving costs.
Compare.limitCity: Figures describe {toCity} and {fromCity} — the capital or largest city on each side — not the whole country.
Compare.limitVisa: Visa routes, fees and processing times are a snapshot taken at the review date. Only the official authority is authoritative.
Compare.limitJobs: Job entries are role archetypes and demand signals, not vacancies, and salary ranges are not offers.
Compare.sourcesDates: Cost data reviewed {costDate}. {to} visa information reviewed {guideDate}.
Compare.outsideWidensSlightly: Living outside the centre saves about {saving} a month in {toCity}, bringing the essential budget to {toCost}. It saves proportionally more in {fromCity}, so the gap edges up from {centrePercent}% to {outsidePercent}%.

Data.title: Data & sources behind every TRAVLBOK figure
Data.subtitle: Every source behind TRAVLBOK: 4 cost-of-living datasets, 13 official immigration authorities, what each figure measures and what the numbers leave out.
Data.reviewed: Cost dataset last reviewed end to end on {date}.
Data.coverageBody: Counted from the live dataset at build time, so this table cannot drift from what the site actually serves.
Data.measuredBody: Every cost figure is a monthly average for the country capital or largest city, expressed in US dollars so countries stay directly comparable.
Data.officialSourcesBody: Linked from each country guide. These are authoritative on fees and processing times; our figures are a snapshot taken at the review date.
Data.limitsIntro: Stated plainly, because a number without its caveats is worse than no number:
Data.limitNotAdvice: TRAVLBOK is not an immigration adviser and has no government affiliation. Nothing here is legal advice.
Data.limitEstimates: Cost figures are estimates for shortlisting, not quotes. Prices vary by neighbourhood, season and household.
